NVDA: Kyber rack for Rubin Ultra reportedly slips
View: According to SemiAnalysis, NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 rack, meant for 2027's
Rubin Ultra, will be delayed more than 12 months to 2028 on manufacturing
problems with the copper "orthogonal" PCB midplane that carries the NVLink
fabric (signal-integrity, power, and thermal challenges as layer counts rise). NVIDIA
also reportedly killed the NVL72x2 stopgap after large customers balked, and the
source_file: data/inputs/reports/INTEL/20260707-Wedbush-Hardware：Daily Views on Tech Headlines  NVDA， INTC， Huawei， FMS.pdf

text:
optics-based NVL576 may slip or ship in low volume, since a production-ready
co-packaged-optics NVSwitch is not expected before the post-Rubin Feynman
generation; 2026 Rubin parts on the existing Oberon rack are unaffected. Per press
reports, Nvidia has denied SemiAnalysis's conclusions.
Various speculation around Rubin Ultra concerns/delays has seemingly been
proliferating since GTC (packaging, die count, memory, and now backplane
concerns). With the product not due till 2H'27, we would expect some flexibility
as NVDA works through the design process, with arguably the challenge having
more to do with: 1) the increased scrutiny around NVDA designs given the
source_file: data/inputs/reports/INTEL/20260707-Wedbush-Hardware：Daily Views on Tech Headlines  NVDA， INTC， Huawei， FMS.pdf

text:
implications for technology direction and the supply chain and 2) the extended
product roadmap NVDA is providing to investors we believe in part due to the
increased scrutiny around NVDA's technology direction.
Net, while NVDA's progress with Rubin Ultra is certainly something that needs to be
monitored (particularly given supply chain implications tied to technology timing
and direction), we believe it's too early to be concerned around potential NVDA
delays for products that aren't due for another 12 to 18 months. Tom's Hardware
INTC: More CPU price increases?
View: Tom's Hardware suggests that both Intel Xeon and Core Ultra parts saw list
source_file: data/inputs/reports/INTEL/20260707-Wedbush-Hardware：Daily Views on Tech Headlines  NVDA， INTC， Huawei， FMS.pdf

text:
price increases at the start of the 3rd quarter. Given continued shortages of server
CPUs in particular, we see room for Intel to lift pricing without affecting demand.
The question rather is whether OEM PX is seeing changes that parallel list price
increases or whether Intel is only shifting distribution/retail pricing (a much smaller
portion of Intel's business). Tom's HardwareHuawei, Chip Design: Huawei's Tau
Scaling Law V2 details a 3D "LogicFolding" path, extending to Ascend AI chips
View: Per TrendForce (citing Chinese media and Huawei's ChinaXiv paper),
Huawei's updated Tau Scaling Law lays out, pre "Logic Folding," which stacks

transistor density and -41% power at a fixed node, validated first on the Kirin 2026

around 2030, enabled by low-temperature hybrid bonding.

place in Santa Clara from August 4th to 6th. We will be hosting in person investor meetings
(centered around FMS and at company HQs close to the conference). Confirmed participants so far

Risks to the Attainment of Our Price Targets and Ratings: Hardware
●
Shifts in competition, pricing, technology, and macroeconomic conditions.
●
Changes in hyperscale spending tied to shifts in growth or increased optimization.
●
Unforeseen events affecting production capacity (power outages, fires, storms, etc.).
●
Shifts in worldwide trade conditions that lead to macro instability and or close certain markets.
●
Increased competition from China based manufacturers entering new markets.
